action_items: OPTIONAL nit: there is no DELETE /api/dev-projects/{id} endpoint. The review-request explicitly asks 'PLEASE DELETE these test projects and their dev_code_files/dev_prod_releases at the end'. Cleanup fixtures cannot use HTTP so I cleaned up directly via MongoDB (dev_projects + dev_code_files + dev_prod_releases). If regular users need to delete projects, this endpoint should exist.

OPTIONAL nit: dev_publish.py _dns_proof_sync only checks CNAME + TXT — it doesn't fall back to A/AAAA records or CNAME chains beyond one hop. Good enough for the current tokenised model but worth noting if you later support apex domain proof via A record.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/dev_publish.py _dns_proof_sync: catches bare Exception on both dns.resolver.resolve calls — this masks NXDOMAIN vs SERVFAIL vs Timeout. In pathological cases (e.g., resolver misconfig) users would see 'No matching record' forever with no way to tell it's a transient DNS error. Consider distinguishing dns.resolver.NXDOMAIN / NoAnswer / Timeout in the detail string for better debuggability.

routes/dev_publish.py PATCH production line 240: domain_verify_token uses new_id().split('-')[0] — that's 8 hex chars of entropy (32 bits). For a proof-of-ownership token this is fine (attacker would need to hijack DNS anyway) but a full uuid4 hex or urlsafe(16) would cost nothing extra and is more defensible.

services/dev_preview_shim.py PREVIEW_CSP includes 'unsafe-inline' for both script-src and style-src. Understandable because LLM-generated apps almost always emit inline scripts, but this partially defeats CSP. Long-term: consider a nonce-per-response scheme (harder because the shim itself is inline) or CSP report-only for tighter policies.
services/dev_chat_ideas.py: NEW FILE — clean split of 5 functions, no circular imports observed. LGTM.

services/dev_os_templates.py: the _CODE_TEMPLATES map is mutated onto the TEMPLATES list at module import time. Works, but a bit magical; a class method or explicit registration in each template dict would be more discoverable.

GET /api/p-resolve line 319 fires DNS resolution SYNCHRONOUSLY (via to_thread) on every unauthenticated request for an unconnected domain. Potential thundering-herd if a user's DNS is misconfigured and the p-resolve endpoint is polled by their frontend bootstrap in a loop. Consider caching the last DNS check result for N seconds (e.g., 60s) keyed by custom_domain.
